claim: mobjinfo[NUMMOBJTYPES] OOB read flagged after the doomednum-match loop (p_mobj.c:623,767)
rationale: Both sites are guarded by 'if (i==NUMMOBJTYPES) I_Error(...)' immediately before the mobjinfo[i] access; I_Error ends in exit(-1) (noreturn). cppcheck does not model the C11 _Noreturn keyword on the i_system.h prototype, so it assumes I_Error returns and reports a phantom OOB. Code is correct.

claim: player->ammo[NUMAMMO]/ammo[-1] OOB flagged in P_GiveAmmo (p_inter.c:87)
rationale: Guarded by 'if (ammo < 0
topic: | ammo >= NUMAMMO) I_Error(...)' (DOOM-0021 fixed the >NUMAMMO off-by-one to >=). I_Error is noreturn (exit -1) but cppcheck does not model C11 _Noreturn, so it cannot see the guard short-circuits the access. cppcheck's own 'condition redundant OR index accessed' wording confirms the guard. Code is correct.|cppcheck-noreturn-not-modeled

claim: s_sound.c:665 uninitvar 'music' in S_ChangeMusic
rationale: music is set in the if/else at 657-663: the bad-number branch calls I_Error (exit -1, _Noreturn), the else assigns &S_music[musicnum]. So music is always initialised at line 665. cppcheck does not model C11 _Noreturn, so it cannot see the I_Error branch never falls through. Same blind spot as p_mobj/p_inter. Code is correct.

claim: i_sound.c:346 negativeIndex vol_lookup[leftvol*256] in I_SetChannels/updateSoundParams
rationale: leftvol is clamped at 341-342: 'if (leftvol < 0 || leftvol > 127) I_Error(...)'. I_Error is _Noreturn, so leftvol is in [0,127] at line 346 and vol_lookup[leftvol*256] is in range. cppcheck cannot model the noreturn guard. Code is correct.

claim: p_enemy.c:381-382 nullPointer actor->target in P_NewChaseDir
rationale: actor->target is null-checked at 375-376: 'if (!actor->target) I_Error(...)'. I_Error is _Noreturn, so actor->target is non-null when dereferenced at 381-382. cppcheck cannot model the noreturn guard. Code is correct.

claim: p_mobj.c:306 shiftNegativeLHS 'mo->player->deltaviewheight = mo->momz>>3'
rationale: momz is fixed_t (signed). The arithmetic right shift of a negative value is the intended fixed-point divide-toward-negative-infinity for the landing squat. On every platform DOOM targets (two's complement, gcc) >> on a negative int is an arithmetic shift. Replacing with /8 would change rounding (toward zero) and alter the squat feel. Intentional original DOOM behaviour - do not touch.

claim: p_pspr.c:530 integerOverflow '-0x40000000/20' (ANG90) in A_Saw turn-to-face
rationale: ANG90 is 0x40000000 (angle_t). The expression 'angle - player->mo->angle' is deliberate unsigned angle_t wrap arithmetic compared against signed -ANG90/20; the values do not actually overflow at runtime (-0x40000000/20 = -53687091, well within int). This is load-bearing original DOOM angle math used identically in every port. Touching it would break the chainsaw turn-to-face. Intentional - do not touch.

claim: r_things.c:438 negativeIndex patch->columnofs[texturecolumn] in R_DrawVisSprite
rationale: The range check at 433-436 is under '#ifdef RANGECHECK'. In release builds texturecolumn is kept in range by the upstream vis->x1/x2 clamping in R_ProjectSprite, exactly as in vanilla DOOM and Chocolate Doom. Adding an unconditional clamp here would change renderer behaviour (skip columns vanilla would draw). Project goal is to keep original DOOM rendering. Leave as-is.

claim: am_map.c:411 integerOverflow 'max_x - min_x' in AM_findMinMaxBoundaries
rationale: min_x/max_x are seeded with MAXINT/-MAXINT then narrowed to real vertex coordinates by the loop at 398-409. A loaded map always has vertices, and map coords are bounded far below MAXINT, so the subtraction never underflows in practice. cppcheck assumes the worst-case seed range. Theoretical only; vanilla code. Leave as-is.

claim: p_switch.c:123 arrayIndexOutOfBounds alphSwitchList[41] accessed at index 49 in P_InitSwitchList
rationale: The loop `for (i=0; i<MAXSWITCHES; i++)` (MAXSWITCHES=50, p_spec.h:241) reads alphSwitchList[i].episode and `break`s on the terminator entry {"\0","\0",0} (episode==0) which sits at index 41 in the 42-entry literal. So i never exceeds 41 at runtime; index 49 is cppcheck's worst-case loop-bound assumption ignoring the in-bounds terminator. Vanilla DOOM; safe as long as the terminator stays within MAXSWITCHES, which it does.

claim: f_finale.c:626 arrayIndexOutOfBoundsCond patch->columnofs[8] accessed at index 319 in F_DrawPatchCol
rationale: columnofs is a flexible-array-member declared `int columnofs[8]` in patch_t (r_defs.h) as a placeholder; the real length equals the patch's width. F_BunnyScroll draws the 320-wide END/bunny patches, so columnofs has 320 real entries and index 319 is in range. cppcheck assumes the declared placeholder size 8. Same flexible-array class as r_things.c columnofs. Vanilla; safe.

claim: d_main.c:613 nullPointerRedundantCheck home in IdentifyVersion (sprintf basedefault from $HOME)
rationale: `home = getenv("HOME"); if (!home) I_Error(...)` guards the subsequent use. I_Error is _Noreturn (i_system.h, DOOM-0023), so home is non-null at the sprintf. cppcheck does not model C11 _Noreturn so it treats the !home branch as fall-through. Same noreturn blind spot as the p_mobj/p_inter/s_sound ledger entries. Code is correct.

claim: i_net.c:237 & i_net.c:318 nullPointerRedundantCheck '!hostentry' (gethostbyname result deref)
rationale: Both sites are `hostentry = gethostbyname(...); if (!hostentry) I_Error(...); ...hostentry->h_addr_list...`. I_Error is _Noreturn (i_system.h, DOOM-0023), so hostentry is non-null at the deref. cppcheck does not model C11 _Noreturn — same blind spot as the p_mobj/p_inter/s_sound/d_main ledger entries. Code is correct.

claim: p_doors.c:223 identicalConditionAfterEarlyExit '!p' second condition always false in EV_DoLockedDoor
rationale: EV_DoLockedDoor early-exits with `p = thing->player; if (!p) return 0;` before the switch, so the per-case `if (!p) return 0;` guards are redundant (always false). This is verbatim vanilla linuxdoom-1.10 code — id left the per-case checks in. Harmless dead redundancy, not a bug; project keeps original DOOM behaviour. Leave as-is.

claim: g_game.c:1466 redundantAssignment 'viewactive' reassigned before use in G_InitNew
rationale: G_InitNew sets `viewactive = true;` at ~1461 then again at ~1466. The duplicate is verbatim vanilla linuxdoom-1.10 (id's original G_InitNew). Behaviour-neutral; assigning true twice has no effect. Not a bug; deleting it is an orthogonal edit to vanilla code (rule 11). Leave as-is.

claim: f_wipe.c:110 knownConditionTrueFalse 'else if (*w < *e)' always true in wipe ColorXForm
rationale: Inside `if (*w != *e) { if (*w > *e) {...} else if (*w < *e) {...} }` the trailing `*w < *e` is provably always true (the two values differ and the >-branch was taken otherwise). cppcheck is technically right, but it's vanilla linuxdoom-1.10 defensive code equivalent to a plain `else`. Behaviour-correct; not a bug. Leave as-is.

claim: semgrep/grep flag ~90 strcpy/sprintf/strcat 'unsafe C function' uses across the engine (d_main.c, g_game.c, m_menu.c, hu_stuff.c, wi_stuff.c, i_sound.c, sndserv, etc.).
rationale: These are regex matches on the function name, not exploitable flows. The DOOM sources copy compile-time string literals (e.g. strcpy(savedescription,\"NET GAME\"), strcpy(name,\"INTERPIC\")) or bounded data (sprintf(name,\"map0%i\",map) with map a small int) into adequately-sized fixed buffers. No attacker-controlled data crosses a trust boundary in a local single-player engine. Per the audit's own PHASE 2, confirm exploitability not keyword match. Reassess only if a specific call takes unbounded external input into an undersized buffer.

claim: [CRITICAL] Command injection: i_sound.c:791 sndserver = popen(buffer, "w").
rationale: buffer is built from sndserver_filename (compile-time default "./sndserver ", overridable only via the user's own default.cfg "sndserver" var) plus the user's own $DOOMWADDIR env, then "-quiet". This is how DOOM launches its own sound-server child process by design; all inputs are local and self-controlled in a single-player engine. No untrusted/remote data reaches the command. Not attacker-reachable. (The whole legacy sndserver path is also superseded by SDL2 audio, DOOM-0004.)

claim: cppcheck: Array 'mobjinfo[137]' accessed at index 137 (out of bounds) at p_mobj.c:623 (P_RespawnSpecials) and p_mobj.c:767 (P_SpawnMapThing).
rationale: Same class as the existing p_inter.c noreturn entry. Each access is immediately preceded by 'for(i=0;i<NUMMOBJTYPES;i++) ...; if(i==NUMMOBJTYPES) I_Error(...)'. I_Error is _Noreturn (DOOM-0023) so i<NUMMOBJTYPES is guaranteed at the mobjinfo[i] access, but cppcheck does not model I_Error as noreturn and so treats i==137 as reachable. The DOOM-0020 guard is present and correct. Code is correct.

claim: ~90 MAJOR strcpy/strcat/sprintf "unsafe C function" + semgrep findings across linuxdoom-1.10 (d_main.c, g_game.c, m_menu.c, m_misc.c, hu_stuff.c, i_sound.c, d_net.c, sndserv/) indicate buffer-overflow risk.
rationale: False positives: all are faithful 1997 id Software calls copying STRING LITERALS (e.g. DEVDATA"default.cfg", "NET GAME", EMPTYSTRING, "ds%s"+8-char WAD lump names) or bounded inputs into buffers sized to hold them; no attacker-influenced unbounded source reaches them. Verified by data-flow tracing. The project preserves id's code verbatim and only fixes genuinely-reachable overflows. The ONE real exception (G_RecordDemo, g_game.c:1553, unbounded -record CLI arg into demoname[32]) was fixed under DOOM-0070. Do not re-flag the literal/bounded calls.

claim: [CRITICAL] Command Injection — i_sound.c:794 sndserver = popen(buffer, "w").
rationale: False positive: the popen call lives in the legacy SNDSERV external-sound-server block which is NOT compiled in the modern build (no -DSNDSERV in the Makefile; audio is SDL2_mixer). The block is dead code; `buffer` is built from a fixed internal sndserver path, not attacker input, even if it were compiled. Unreachable -> not exploitable.

claim: [MINOR] CMake find_package without version floor (mingw-deps/Vulkan-Headers/.../CMakeLists.txt:13) and 14 [MINOR] Debug/Temp-Code findings.
rationale: False positives / out of scope: all live under mingw-deps/ (vendored upstream Vulkan-Headers + SDL2 dev libs, regenerable per mingw-deps/README.md, gitignored) — not project source. The one in-tree debug match (hu_stuff.c:813) is already a commented-out 1997 debug line, harmless. Exclude vendored trees from project audits.

claim: [MAJOR] Continuous Integration Missing — no .github/workflows etc.
rationale: Not a correctness/security defect — an infrastructure choice. The project ships via a hand-run AppImage packaging script and manual GitHub Releases; CI is a possible future enhancement, not an audit fix target. Noted, not actioned.

claim: cppcheck portability: intToPointerCast (p_mobj.c:425,434; p_tick.c:83,108), shiftNegativeLHS (p_mobj.c:306), CastAddressToIntegerAtReturn (d_net.c:93).
rationale:
All vanilla 1997 id code. The int<->pointer casts are DOOM's thinker-function sentinel idiom (function.acp1/acv casts) and packet-address returns; shiftNegativeLHS is vanilla fixed-point math. Correct on the LP64 x86-64 Linux target the project builds for; cppcheck's 'portability' class flags theoretical non-portability, not a defect. Preserve-vanilla; not actionable.</rationale>

claim: cppcheck error: Signed integer overflow for expression '-0x40000000/20' at p_pspr.c:530.
rationale:
Vanilla autoaim turn-to-face code: `-ANG90/20` where ANG90==0x40000000 (angle_t). DOOM angle arithmetic is unsigned 32-bit and relies on wraparound; -0x40000000/20 = -53687091 does not actually overflow int. cppcheck mis-evaluates the constant sub-expression. Verbatim id code; intended DOOM autoaim behaviour. Not a defect.</rationale>

claim: cppcheck error: syntax error at r_vulkan.cpp:6335 [syntaxError].
rationale:
cppcheck cannot fully parse the C++23 Vulkan backend; the file compiles cleanly with g++ -std=c++23 and links into linuxxdoom. A cppcheck C++-frontend limitation, not a code defect -- and it means cppcheck gives no real coverage of r_vulkan.cpp (the indie-review lanes cover it instead). Not actionable.</rationale>

claim: cppcheck style: duplicateAssignExpression ry/nx (r_mesh.c:1083) and shadowVariable 'menuactive' (i_video.c:232,403).
rationale:
r_mesh: ry=-cosf(a) and nx=-cosf(a) are BOTH correctly -cos(a) per the documented camera screen-right (sin a,-cos a) and billboard-normal (-cos a,-sin a) vectors -- a coincidental shared value, not a copy-paste bug. i_video: the two `extern boolean menuactive;` are function-scope extern declarations pulling in the m_menu.c global (idiom to avoid a header include), not locals shadowing it. Both are cppcheck misreading intentional code. Not defects.</rationale>

claim: commits.md:46 "push after each logical batch" conflicts with global CLAUDE.md rule 6's "push after each release" (flagged CRITICAL push-cadence conflict).
rationale: Not a conflict. Global CLAUDE.md rule 6 gives PUBLIC repos unlimited free CI minutes and says push freely; the "after each release" cadence is the PRIVATE-repo rule. DOOM_Ants is a public repo (gh visibility PUBLIC; commits.md:46 states "This is a public repo"), so "push after each logical batch" is fully consistent with the global rule. The cold reviewer applied the private-repo clause to a public repo.

claim: dependencies.md:166-170 ("Bump and idiom-refresh ship together") is a near-duplicate of global CLAUDE.md rule 5b and should be reduced to a one-line reference.
rationale: Not project-internal duplication. The "other doc" is the user's PRIVATE global ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md, which is not in the DOOM_Ants repo and is not shipped to contributors. A contributor who clones the repo needs this rule stated in dependencies.md; replacing it with a reference to a machine-local file they do not have would break the standard. Cold-eyes dedup applies to intra-project duplication only.

claim: renderer.md misc5 push-constant row lists z/w as reserved but they are in use (de-tile quality / dirt-colour / filth toggle); table needs updating.
rationale: Stale-roadmap echo. The reviewer read ROADMAP bullet DOOM-0194 ("Fix the stale misc5 push-constant comment in pathtrace.comp"), which is already ✅ shipped (ROADMAP.md:1807). Verified directly: renderer.md's misc5 table row already lists all four components (x=grime id, y=de-tile quality, z=dirt-colour id, w=filth toggle) and pathtrace.comp's misc5 struct comment (lines ~259-264) matches. Nothing says "reserved". No current defect.

claim: cppcheck selfAssignment: header.numlumps/infotableofs (w_wad.c:206,207,285) and mt->x/y/angle/type/options + blockmaplump[i] (p_setup.c:342-346,481) are redundant self-assignments
rationale: These are DOOM's endian-swap macros, not assignments: LONG()/SHORT() (m_swap.h) expand to the identity on little-endian, which is what cppcheck sees, and to a byte-swap on big-endian. Removing them silently breaks big-endian portability of WAD directory and map-thing parsing. Correct as written.

claim: cppcheck error at p_switch.c:123 — Array 'alphSwitchList[41]' accessed at index 49, out of bounds (MAXSWITCHES is 50)
rationale: alphSwitchList terminates with a sentinel row {"\0","\0",0} and the loop breaks on !alphSwitchList[i].episode before i can exceed 40 (p_switch.c:121-127). cppcheck models the i < MAXSWITCHES bound but not the sentinel, so the flagged path is unreachable. Verified by reading the array tail and the loop.

claim: cppcheck: mus2mid.c:402 condition 'controllernumber < 1' is always false — redundant check
rationale: True but deliberate. controllernumber is an unsigned byte and the ==0 case is handled by the preceding branch, so <1 is indeed unreachable — it is the lower half of an explicit bounds guard (controllernumber < 1 || > 9) on the controller_map[] index, in code hardened against malformed MUS lumps (DOOM-0093). Dropping half a bounds check to satisfy a style rule makes the guard read as one-sided and is a bad trade in a security path.

claim: [via /debt-sweep doc lane] DOOM-0205 (Render Effects submenu) is still 🚧 although its code is fully present in m_menu.c — stale roadmap status, should be flipped to ✅
rationale: Not drift. The bullet's own body states the remaining gate: "Menu navigation is Wayland-input-gated so on-screen visual check is the user's". 🚧 here means code-complete but awaiting user visual sign-off — the same convention DOOM-0183 uses ("graduates to shipped when it clears its hardware play-test"). Flipping it would assert a verification that has not happened. Leave 🚧 until the user confirms on screen.

claim: [via /debt-sweep doc lane] d_main.c:1356 comment cites DOOM-0093 but the -warp bounds fix shipped as DOOM-0219 — wrong ID, should be corrected
rationale: Half true, rejected as stated. All 11 hardening comments (w_wad.c, d_net.c, i_net.c, i_sound.c, p_spec.c, d_main.c, mus2mid.c/.h, mus2mid_test.cpp) cite DOOM-0093 consistently as the umbrella research item that motivated the 2026-07-23 pass; re-pointing one site makes it inconsistent with ten siblings, and re-pointing all eleven needs a per-site ID mapping with real risk of mis-attribution. Resolved instead on the roadmap side: DOOM-0093 annotated 2026-07-26 to state that the CPU-side subset shipped as DOOM-0212..0220 and that its own remaining scope is the GPU axis.

claim: nee_sampling_test's estimator tolerance makes it an intermittent CI flake — roughly 1 spurious failure in 10,000 runs for the "dominant" weight set.
rationale: The thin margin was real and is fixed, but the FLAKE framing is wrong and should not be re-raised. tests/nee_sampling_test.cpp seeds its PRNG with a fixed constant (seed = 0x1234567u) and nee_sampling.h's pcgHash is pure 32-bit integer arithmetic, so a given binary draws the identical 16M-sample sequence on every run; TEST_CXXFLAGS carries no -ffast-math/-ffp-contract/-march=native, so the double-precision accumulation is reproducible too. A build that passes always passes and a build that fails always fails — there is no per-run randomness for a 1-in-10,000 tail to act on. The measured margins (3.89 sigma "dominant", 4.06 sigma "skewed", computed from Var(X)=sum g^2/pdf - (sum g)^2) describe brittleness under a future change to N, the weights or g — not run-to-run instability. Fixed 2026-07-26 by deriving the bound from the exact variance at 6 sigma; observed distance is now 0.98-1.54 sigma across all five sets.

claim: Add a parallel tests/*_test.c lane built with $(CC) so the .c units (mus2mid.c, rb_image.c, rb_text.c, iwad_detect.h) are exercised as C, matching the object the game ships.
rationale: The underlying OBSERVATION is true and is now written into docs/standards/testing.md as a known limit of the harness: tests are .cpp, so a .c unit under test is recompiled as C++23 by g++ while the shipping object is gnu11 via gcc. The proposed REMEDY is dismissed and should not be re-proposed. A second build lane would double the Makefile's test machinery and break the harness's load-bearing property ("adding a test is one file, no Makefile edit") to guard a divergence that has never produced a defect here: the units in question are self-contained parsers and index math with no overload resolution, no implicit void* conversions in their own bodies, and no C/C++ linkage surface (rb_image.h and rb_text.h already self-guard with extern "C"). The residual risk is covered by the DOOM-0203 headless boot smoke, which runs the real gcc-built objects on a real WAD. Revisit only if a real bug is ever traced to the language difference.

claim: cppcheck error at p_pspr.c:530 — "Signed integer overflow for expression '-0x40000000/20'"
rationale: Two-part dismissal. (1) The arithmetic claim is simply wrong: ANG90 is 0x40000000 (tables.h:69), an int constant; -0x40000000 = -1073741824 is representable in int32 (min -2147483648) and /20 = -53687091. No overflow occurs. (2) The interesting part of that line — `angle - player->mo->angle < -ANG90/20` compares an angle_t (unsigned) against a negative int, so the int converts to 4241243085u and the test is almost always true — is verbatim 1997 id Software behaviour in A_Saw's turn-to-target logic. It affects demo playback and gameplay feel, so it is deliberately retained (same posture as the rest of the vanilla gameplay tree, whose style-finding policy is DOOM-0249). Do not "fix" either half.

claim: bandit + cppcheck findings inside mingw-deps/ (Vulkan-Headers registry Python, SDL2 test programs) and the vendored stb_*.h single-header libraries
rationale: Not this project's code. mingw-deps/ is a staged snapshot of upstream SDL2 / SDL2_mixer / Vulkan-Headers used only for the Windows cross-build (see docs/standards/dependencies.md); linuxdoom-1.10/stb_image.h, stb_image_write.h and stb_truetype.h are vendored public-domain single-header libraries. Findings there (bandit B404/B603 on Vulkan-Headers' generator scripts, shiftTooManyBitsSigned in SDL2's testatomic.c, memleak/nullPointerArithmeticOutOfMemory in stb) are upstream's to fix and must not be patched locally — a local edit would be silently reverted by the next dependency refresh. The correct remedy is an audit scope exclusion for mingw-deps/ and the stb_* headers, not a code change. Re-raise only if we ever fork one of those upstreams.

claim: contract_doc_drift: "doc references `X` but no match in project sources" for file:line-range citations (e.g. `r_defs.h:101-135`), Ants-MCP verb names (`roadmap_query`, `audit_run`), roadmap slugs and placeholder tokens (`DOOM-NNNN`, `NNNN-topic.md`)
rationale: Detector limitation, not drift: 517 of the sweep's findings are this shape and the ones spot-checked are all resolvable. `r_defs.h:101-135` is a line-range citation into a file that exists — the detector greps for the literal string "r_defs.h:101-135" in sources and cannot find it by construction. `roadmap_query` / `audit_run` / `changelog_log` / `audit_falsepos_log` are Ants-MCP tool names quoted by the house standards; they are not project symbols and never will be. `DOOM-NNNN`, `ANTS-NNNN`, `NNNN-topic.md`, `Kind:`, `Layman:`, `phase-2-the-spin` are format placeholders and roadmap slugs. Genuine code-vs-doc drift is found by the indie-review docs lane (six real items fixed under DOOM-0263 on 2026-07-26), which requires a doc citation AND contradicting code evidence. Treat this rule's output as noise unless a specific finding names a symbol that genuinely no longer exists.

claim: cppcheck knownConditionTrueFalse: r_vulkan.cpp:7831,7832 'BOUNCES&1' is always true (GI bake ping-pong buffer selection)
rationale: BOUNCES is `const int BOUNCES = 3` on r_vulkan.cpp:7830, so `BOUNCES&1` is literally always true — cppcheck is right about the expression and wrong about it being a defect. The 6-line comment immediately above (7824-7829) states the intent: the ping-pong must start on whichever buffer makes the FINAL bounce land in probeBuf, "for an odd bounce count that means starting the write on probeBuf". The parity test is the mechanism that keeps this correct if BOUNCES is retuned; folding it to a constant would silently break the buffer choice the moment anyone sets BOUNCES=2 or 4. Deliberate, documented generality. Code is correct.

claim: cppcheck redundantAssignment: r_vulkan.cpp:4924 'rs.polygonMode' reassigned before the old value is used (RT weapon-overlay pipeline)
rationale: The comment at r_vulkan.cpp:4918-4923 pre-empts the checker verbatim: "rs is FILL and pDepthStencilState is left at &ds by the blocks above, but set both explicitly so this stays correct regardless of the wire branch." The DOOM-0170 L2a overlay pipeline must be FILL + depth-on irrespective of which earlier branch (wireframe debug view) last touched `rs`; the redundancy is the invariant. Removing it couples this pipeline's correctness to an unrelated debug toggle. Code is correct.

claim: cppcheck knownConditionTrueFalse: r_mesh.c:789 condition 'ulen<1e-6f' is always false in RB_SunHeading
rationale: ulen is computed from the compile-time constants RB_SUN_DIR_X/Y (r_mesh.c:781), so at the shipped tune it can never be under 1e-6 — cppcheck is right about the current constants. The 6-line comment at r_mesh.c:783-788 states exactly this and why the guard stays: "Not a state the shipped constant can reach; the guard is one line and a NaN would propagate through the whole field and then through sigma." A divide-by-zero here would poison the entire seep/fog field rather than fail locally. One-line guard against a retune of a constant. Code is correct.

claim: semgrep insecure-use-string-copy-fn + cppcheck memsetClassFloat: rb_materials.h:40,63,76,77,85 (material CSV parser)
rationale: All four copies are bounded strncpy with the destination NUL-terminated, verified against the rb_matrow_t definition at rb_materials.h:48-54: :40 and :63 are strncpy(buf, src, sizeof(buf)-1) followed on the same line by buf[sizeof(buf)-1]='\0'; :77 is strncpy(out->name, ..., 8) into char name[9] followed by out->name[8]='\0'; :85 writes at most sizeof-1 into maps[i] whose tail byte was already zeroed by the memset on :76. The memsetClassFloat on :76 concerns out->uv_scale, which is IEEE-754 (all-zero bits = 0.0f on both shipped targets) and is unconditionally overwritten on :88 before any read. No overflow and no unterminated string is reachable.

claim: cppcheck badBitmaskCheck: m_menu.c:880 operator '|' with one operand equal to zero is redundant (open(name, O_RDONLY|0, 0666))
rationale: Verified at m_menu.c:880: this is id Software's original 1997 M_ReadSaveStrings line, unchanged by this fork. O_RDONLY is 0 on Linux, so `O_RDONLY | 0` is a no-op — cosmetically redundant, behaviourally identical, and it cannot be a defect because both operands are zero. Editing it would be a drive-by reformat of vanilla code (global CLAUDE.md rule 11) with no behavioural gain. Code is correct.

claim: cppcheck duplicateAssignExpression: r_mesh.c:1904 same expression '-cosf(a)' used in consecutive assignments of 'ry' and 'nx' in RB_BuildSprites (re-fire; ledger entry cites the pre-move line 1083)
rationale: Verified at r_mesh.c:1903-1905. ry is the Y component of the camera-right vector (sin a, -cos a, 0); nx is the X component of the billboard normal (-cos a, -sin a, 0) pointing at the eye. Two independent geometric quantities from two different vectors that coincide in value at this basis, as the two inline comments on those lines state. Collapsing them into one variable would couple the billboard normal to the right vector and break the moment either derivation changes. Same finding as the existing ledger entry for r_mesh.c:1083; only the line number moved. Code is correct.

claim: cppcheck unreadVariable: r_vulkan.cpp:6288 variable 'used' is assigned a value that is never used (final 'used += lverts' in the menu text/logo draw)
rationale: Verified at r_vulkan.cpp:6280-6289: `used` is the running vertex-buffer offset threaded through a sequence of queued draws, and the flagged statement is the last one's post-increment, so nothing reads it before the function returns. Keeping the accumulator's invariant complete is what makes it safe to append a further draw block after it; dropping the final increment would leave a stale offset as a trap for the next edit. Zero-cost, and the alternative is a latent bug. Code is correct.

claim: Unchecked return values on vkUnmapMemory (r_vulkan.cpp:1762) and vkDestroySemaphore (r_vulkan.cpp:1589)
rationale: Both functions are declared to return void in the Vulkan 1.3 API (vkUnmapMemory: "void vkUnmapMemory(VkDevice, VkDeviceMemory)"; vkDestroySemaphore likewise). There is no VkResult to test, so the finding describes an impossible edit — Check() cannot wrap either call, and the surrounding code's use of Check() on the genuinely VkResult-returning calls (vkMapMemory on the line immediately above 1762) is the correct and complete pattern. Any re-raise of "unchecked Vulkan call" must first confirm the function actually returns VkResult.

claim: CRITICAL CPU/GPU race: BuildFrameInputs writes the single-copy g.emitBuf / g.sprWorldBuf before the fence when buildAhead is true
rationale: The buffers really are single-copy (r_vulkan.cpp:9095 says so) and build-ahead really does run before the fence, but no GPU work reads them on a raster frame: emitBuf/sprWorldBuf feed BuildSpriteTlas, RecordRtTrace, RunGiBake and RB_RtVerify, none of which is recorded when rtActive is false, and buildAhead is gated on !rtActive. The RT-to-raster transition is covered separately -- modeChanged forces vkDeviceWaitIdle and suppresses build-ahead for that frame -- so nothing from the previous mode is still in flight. Verified 2026-08-03; the misleading comment that asserted the wrong REASON for this safety ("every buffer it writes is slotted") was corrected in the same pass. NOTE: this dismissal is conditional on the render path, not the allocation — adding a raster-side GPU read of either buffer would make it real.

claim: HIGH zombie feature: descriptor binding 6 (fog-light storage buffer) is declared and pool-allocated but never written by any descriptor write
rationale: Binding 6 is declared in pathtrace.comp:87 as `readonly buffer FogLights` and IS populated — UploadFogLightGrid (r_vulkan.cpp:7592) and BuildFogLightGrid (r_vulkan.cpp:7635) fill and bind it. The reviewing lane was scoped to lines 2441-3960 and both writers sit outside that window, so the absence it observed was an artefact of the partition, not of the code. General lesson for split-file lanes: a "declared but never written" claim cannot be concluded from a line-range slice of the file — grep the whole translation unit before calling a binding dead.

claim: CRITICAL: FloatToHalf (r_vulkan.cpp:3442) maps NaN to 0x7BFF (max finite half) instead of propagating NaN, corrupting the seep field's zLo/zHi
rationale: The behaviour is real and deliberate: the line carries the comment "saturate; never emit an inf", because an inf or NaN in the R16G16B16A16 seep texture poisons the fog march for every sample that reads that cell, whereas a large finite value degrades locally. Reaching it also requires a NaN input, and the one division in the producing path that could generate one (RB_SunHeading, r_mesh.c:789) carries an explicit guard whose own comment states the reason: "a NaN would propagate through the whole field and then through sigma". So the conversion is the second line of defence, not the defect, and the finding demonstrates no reachable NaN.

claim: Four MEDIUM out-of-bounds reads on untrusted WAD data in r_mesh.c: sides[v->vtexside] (1499), spritewidth[lump] in RB_BuildSprites (1960) and RB_BuildPSprites (2118), and segs[ss->firstline] in RB_SectorAtPoint (1894)
rationale: All four indices are validated where they ENTER the engine, so re-checking at use would be dead code. vtexside is assigned at r_mesh.c:294 as `(int)(seg->sidedef - sides)`, and seg->sidedef is itself set at p_setup.c:208 via P_WadIndex(ldef->sidenum[side], numsides, "seg sidedef") — the subtraction can only yield an already-bounded index. The two sprite-lump sites guard `lump < 0` and carry a comment citing R_InstallSpriteLump's load-time validation for the upper bound. The fourth citation does not match the code: r_mesh.c:1894 is RB_WallTexEmits, which opens with an explicit `texnum < 0 || texnum >= numtextures` guard. Verified 2026-08-03 while closing the genuine p_setup.c linedef-vertex gap, so the load-time guard set was read in full during this pass.

claim: clang-tidy clang-analyzer: r_mesh.c:1208/1214/1216/1217 — garbage value, heap out-of-bound access, and uninitialised assign in RB_BuildSeepField's Dijkstra loop.
rationale: The analyzer cannot prove the range invariant on portals[].secA/secB. Both are set at r_mesh.c:1151-1152 as pointer differences from real sector_t* (sg->frontsector - sectors, sg->backsector - sectors), so they are always in [0, numsectors). secFirst is calloc'd with numsectors+1 entries (1162) and secFirst[numsectors] is set at 1177, so secFirst[sec+1] is always in bounds. portals[i].d is written for every i < np at 1155. Every entry pushed onto the heap comes from that same [0,np) range. No path reaches these lines with an out-of-range index.

claim: clang-tidy bugprone-suspicious-realloc-usage: r_mesh.c:93/105/147 — 'b->v'/'b->ssid'/'b->sky' may be set to null if realloc fails, leaking the original buffer.
rationale: All three sites test the result immediately and call I_Error on NULL (r_mesh.c:95-96, 107-108, 149-150). I_Error terminates the process, so the "leaked" original buffer is reclaimed by the OS and no execution continues past the failure. The leak the check describes cannot be observed. This is the engine-wide allocation convention, not an oversight.

claim: clang-tidy bugprone-incorrect-roundings x4: r_vulkan.cpp:6734/6740/6861/6891 — casting (double + 0.5) to integer leads to incorrect rounding; use lround.
rationale: The (int)(x + 0.5f) idiom is only wrong for negative x. All four operands are guarded non-negative: rb_text_width returns 0 unless g.menuFontReady and multiplies a text measurement by a positive scale; rb_text_line_height uses g.menuFont.px_height (a pixel count); rb_menu_cursor_width and rb_menu_logo_width both early-return 0 unless h > 0 and the source dimension > 0, then multiply three non-negative quantities. No negative value can reach the cast.

claim: pyright reportAttributeAccessIssue: hero_ao.py:41 — "LANCZOS" is not a known attribute of module "PIL.Image".
rationale: Measured against the installed Pillow 12.3.0: `from PIL import Image; Image.LANCZOS` evaluates to 1. The top-level alias still exists at runtime and is only absent from the type stub, so this is a stub gap rather than a code defect. The script runs. Re-open only if a Pillow release actually removes the alias, which would be a runtime AttributeError rather than a type error.

claim: shellcheck SC2329 (windows-smoke.sh:135 'cleanup' never invoked) and SC2016 x2 (ci-local.sh:145,150 expressions don't expand in single quotes).
rationale: SC2329: cleanup() is invoked by `trap cleanup EXIT` at windows-smoke.sh:141 — shellcheck does not treat a trap as a call site. SC2016: ci-local.sh:145,150 sit inside the single-quoted script passed to `podman/docker run ... bash -euc`, so the $(...) and $1 must be left unexpanded by the HOST shell and evaluated inside the container. Expanding them there is exactly the bug the single quotes prevent; the one value that IS wanted from the host, "$DEPS_FILE", is deliberately spliced out of the quoting.

claim: ruff B023 x2 (pbr_derive.py:231, hs() does not bind loop variables y/x), ruff S603 (stage_hero.py:46 magick subprocess), vulture (pbr_derive.py:317 unused variable 'sprite'), cppcheck uninitMemberVarNoCtor x2 (save_bounds_test.cpp:26,27).
rationale: B023: hs() is called on lines 232-233 within the same loop iteration that defines it and is never stored, returned or deferred, so late binding cannot be observed. S603 at stage_hero.py:46: magick() is the deliberate ImageMagick shell-out that is the script's whole purpose; its argv comes from the script's own CLI args, not untrusted input. vulture 'sprite': it is a documented reserved PARAMETER of derive_albedo (docstring: "v1 has no sprite derive rows, so this is the plain-RGB path"), not a dead local; removing it changes the signature. cppcheck Cursor::p/end: the single construction site is aggregate-init `Cursor c{buf, buf + len}` at save_bounds_test.cpp:66, which sets both members.

claim: Remaining clang-tidy noise: r_mesh.c:1061 malloc(0) / :1716 calloc(0); r_vulkan.cpp:5983 misplaced-widening-cast; r_mesh.h:30 reserved identifier __R_MESH__; suspicious #include of a .c file in tests/{mus2mid,rb_image,rb_text}_test.cpp; rb_materials.h:87 unchecked atof. Plus acti…
rationale: malloc(0)/calloc(0) are reachable only for an empty cell set or an empty atlas, are legal C, and both results are NULL-checked. r_vulkan.cpp:5983: id*3+2 is bounded by the texture count (well under INT_MAX) and a negative would cast to a huge size_t that fails the < out.size() guard safely. __R_MESH__ is the include-guard convention every 1997 DOOM header uses; changing one header alone is worse than leaving it. The tests deliberately #include the .c unit under test (the project's documented single-file test pattern — no Makefile edit, per CLAUDE.md). rb_materials.h:87 atof is immediately range-guarded: `if (out->uv_scale <= 0.0f) out->uv_scale = 1.0f;`. actionlint SC2046: the word-splitting of $(awk ...) is what produces the package list. yamllint: line-length 80, document-start and truthy are unconfigured library defaults this project never adopted, and `on:` is required spelling for a GitHub Actions workflow — a .yamllint declaring the project's real style is the fix, not edits.
